name: og_33_chemically_coupled_growth_and_division
description: Gate D first half: couples study 32's self-maintaining protocell to amphiphile-driven membrane growth and division at a MEASURED critical-geometry (reduced-volume) threshold (hanczyc/budin; ⚑2 Option B, NOT CG membrane mechanics - that is og-33a). Membrane area grows from the metabolism's productive flux; at the measured critical reduced volume the compartment divides (geometry, not an imposed rule). coupled=False is the growth-decoupled null (fixed amphiphile supply); imposed_division=True is the imposed-rule null. Daughters viable only if they resume study-32 self-maintenance. Metabolism = sustained A1 network, NOT autocatalytic (A2 refuted).

network.doc:
Rule-generated open C/H/O reaction universe integrated by the real
libRoadRunner engine; motifs detected post hoc, never declared.

_contract.summary: Rule-generated C1-C3 reaction universe (Wolos-2020-style rules, eQuilibrator dG', catalyst limits) as a libRoadRunner CSTR; autocatalysis detected post hoc.
_contract.description: Every linear C/H/O skeleton up to max_carbons is enumerated and nine prebiotic reaction rules (H2 reductions, enol and reductive carboxylation, aldol/retro-aldol, aldose-ketose isomerisation, alpha/beta decarboxylation, Cannizzaro) are applied exhaustively; each generated reaction is reversible with k_r = k_f exp(dG'/RT) from the vg-data reaction_universe potentials (eQuilibrator component contribution), carries a catalyst class whose shared site pool saturates with organic load, and every species degrades to tar and washes out. The SBML is compiled and advanced each tick by libRoadRunner under vent-buffered CO2/H2 and CSTR organic feeds. Emits the og-02 face observables computed post hoc by a class-agnostic detector (flux-carrying simple cycles with stoichiometric gain > 1), plus the element residual (exact), the integrated carbon-balance residual and the free-energy dissipation.

outputs.net_carbon_flux: net CO2 fixed into organics by internal reactions (mole/second)
outputs.autocatalytic_gain: max over detected motifs of seed production via the cycle / seed loss (dimensionless)
outputs.network_connected: 1 if the alive organic species form one flux-connected network (currency species excluded)
outputs.total_organic_carbon: sum of carbon atoms in organic species (molar C)
outputs.n_autocatalytic_motifs: distinct flux-carrying simple cycles with stoichiometric gain > 1
outputs.dissipation: -sum_r v_r dG_r over internal reactions (watt; >= 0 for consistent kinetics)
outputs.element_residual: max |E S| over internal reactions (exact; 0 for a generated universe)
outputs.carbon_residual: |TOC - TOC0 - (fed + fixed - washed - degraded)| / TOC (integrator tolerance)
outputs.catalyst_saturation: fraction of mineral sites occupied, 1 - f_mineral / sites_mineral

math: v_r = f_cat k0 (F prod[reactants] - R prod[products]),  (F, R) = (1, e^{dG'/RT}) if dG' <= 0 else (e^{-dG'/RT}, 1)
assumptions: Linear carbon skeletons only (no branched acids such as citrate, no alkenes) — rTCA cannot close in this representation; that is a declared v1 limitation.
dG' potentials at the package's pH / ionic strength / temperature (the Phase-1 posterior example point); water activity 1.
Catalyst crowding factors are updated once per tick from the current organic load (operator splitting).

network_ledger.doc:
Element + free-energy ledger over an open chemical network (Phase 3).

Sits beside a ``proto_metabolism`` class and audits, every tick, the three
witnesses the class publishes:

* ``element_residual`` — ``max |E S|`` over the network's internal
  reactions (exact algebra, independent of the integrator): a generated
  universe is balanced by construction; a lumped reaction such as og-02's
  ``OAA + 2 CO2 -> 2 OAA + acetate`` or a rewired null is not, and the
  ledger says so.
* ``carbon_residual`` — the integrated carbon balance
  ``|TOC - TOC0 - (fed + fixed - washed - degraded)| / TOC``, which must stay
  at the integrator's tolerance.
* ``dissipation`` — ``-Σ v_r ΔG_r`` over internal reactions; the second
  law requires it to be non-negative every tick (free-energy
  directionality). ``free_energy_in >= work + dissipated`` of the roadmap
  reduces, for a reactor with no work output, to this inequality.

Publishes the worst-case residuals so far, the directionality witness and
one ``ledger_ok`` flag, mirroring :class:`ConservationLedgerProcess`.

_contract.summary: Element + free-energy ledger over an open reaction network: stoichiometric element residual, integrated carbon balance, dissipation >= 0.
_contract.description: Audits the witnesses a proto_metabolism class publishes each tick: the exact stoichiometric element residual max|E S| (0 for a rule-generated universe; non-zero exposes lumped or rewired reactions that create or destroy atoms), the integrated carbon-balance residual (must sit at integrator tolerance) and the free-energy dissipation -sum v dG (second law: never negative). ledger_ok = 1 while every witness is within tolerance.

outputs.free_energy_directionality: 1 if dissipation has never been below -tolerance
outputs.ledger_ok: 1 if every witness is within tolerance

assumptions: The network class computes the witnesses from its own stoichiometry and live rates; the ledger only accumulates and grades them.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

trap_process.doc:
Real 1-D FiPy finite-volume accumulation column for the Baaske thermal
trap. Reads the pore temperature, the convective flow velocity and the
porosity; derives the thermophoretic + convective accumulation velocity;
solves the steady column with the genuine FiPy FVM solver; and emits the
enrichment factor (read from the solved profile), the residence time and the
FVM balance residual (overwrite sensors — the current state of the trap).

_contract.summary: Real 1-D FiPy accumulation column for the Baaske thermal trap: thermophoresis + convection concentrate a dilute feed, enrichment exponential in pore length.
_contract.description: Derives the accumulation velocity from the pore's thermophoretic (Soret) and convective physics (Pe_conv = flow*width/D; beta = geom*soret*dT*Pe_conv/width * confinement; w_acc = D*beta) and solves the steady 1-D column 0 = D c'' - w_acc c' with the genuine FiPy finite-volume solver (feed at the top, no-flux trapped base). The enrichment factor is READ from the solved base/top ratio (not assigned), reproducing Baaske's exponential length-scaling: >10^8-fold in favorable geometry, ~1 in a no-gradient/no-flow control. All outputs are overwrite sensors; the FVM residual is the spatial-flux-conservation witness.

inputs.flow_velocity: buoyant convective flow speed in the pore (meter/second)
inputs.porosity: pore porosity / openness (dimensionless, 0-1; lower = more confinement = more trapping)

math: beta = geom * soret_coeff * delta_T * Pe_conv / pore_width * (1 - porosity_openness)
0 = D c'' - D*beta c'  ->  enrichment = c_base / c_top = exp(beta * pore_length)
assumptions: Accumulation-column reduced model of the thermal trap (Debye 1939; Baaske 2007): enrichment exponential in pore length.
w_acc from thermophoretic (Soret) drift coupled to buoyant convection; geom calibrates the trap efficiency to the Baaske magnitude.
Steady FVM solve each step (fast relative to pore evolution).
